title: Customer error messaging draft — Hosted overload protection (circuit breakers + load shedding)
content:
Working draft — PM owned
Last edited: 2025-11-06 (post review w/ Support + SRE)
Audience: Customer-facing docs, release notes, Support macros, and status-page incidents.

Goals
- Provide clear, consistent customer-facing language for overload-induced responses (as we introduce hosted circuit breakers + load shedding).
- Make retry behavior predictable (avoid retry storms; encourage backoff + jitter; honor Retry-After).
- Preserve trust: be transparent without over-sharing internal details (avoid “GPU queue depth” in customer-facing copy).
- Ensure messaging works across self-serve Hosted, Hosted Enterprise, and Dedicated (Dedicated: still can hit quota/limits, but messaging should emphasize reserved capacity expectations).

Non-goals
- No pricing/billing promises.
- No guarantee that retries will succeed; we describe best practices.

Terminology to standardize (customer-facing)
- “Overload protection” = a set of safety mechanisms that keep the service reliable under high load.
- “Temporarily overloaded” = short-term capacity saturation; requests may be rejected quickly rather than timing out.
- “Correlation ID / Request ID” = identifier customer can share with Support.
- Avoid: “circuit breaker open”, “shedding”, “brownout”, “token/sec saturation” in customer-facing primary copy (OK for deeper troubleshooting section).

Customer-visible behavior (summary)
1) Under high load, some requests may return explicit overload errors quickly instead of timing out.
2) Responses include:
   - a stable error code
   - a human-readable message
   - a correlation_id
   - retry guidance (Retry-After header when appropriate)
3) Customers should implement:
   - exponential backoff with jitter
   - respecting Retry-After
   - idempotency keys (where applicable) to avoid duplicate work

Error messaging principles
- Be specific about what the client can do next.
- Use “temporary” language for overload and dependencies.
- Avoid implying customer misconfiguration unless we are confident (e.g., 429 rate limit or quota).
- Keep messages short; details go in documentation.

Proposed customer-facing error taxonomy (copy + guidance)
Note: Exact error_code list is defined in ADR-014; below is the external messaging layer.

A) 429 Too Many Requests (Rate limit / concurrency limit)
When used:
- Per-tenant rate limit exceeded
- Per-route concurrency cap exceeded

Primary message (short):
- "Request rate limit exceeded. Please retry after a short delay."

Expanded message (docs/support):
- "You have sent too many requests in a short period, or have exceeded the allowed concurrent requests for this endpoint. Reduce request rate or concurrency and retry using exponential backoff with jitter."

Client action guidance:
- MUST backoff.
- SHOULD respect Retry-After when present.
- SHOULD reduce client-side concurrency.

Status page wording:
- Not typically a status-page event unless widespread + unexpected. Prefer “Operational” and document as normal rate limiting.

B) 503 Service Unavailable (Temporary overload)
When used:
- Regional capacity saturation
- Admission control rejecting to preserve latency SLOs
- Short-term inability to route to capacity

Primary message (short):
- "Service temporarily overloaded. Please retry after a short delay."

Expanded message (docs/support):
- "Redwood is experiencing elevated load in this region or for this model. To maintain reliability, we may reject a portion of requests quickly instead of allowing long timeouts. Retry with exponential backoff and jitter, and honor the Retry-After header."

Client action guidance:
- MUST backoff.
- MUST honor Retry-After when present.
- SHOULD implement max retry time budget (e.g., 30–60s) and fail gracefully.
- SHOULD consider using a fallback model/region if configured (Enterprise feature; docs will link).

Status page wording:
- "We are investigating increased error rates and request rejections for the Hosted API. Some requests may fail with 503 responses indicating temporary overload."

C) 503 Service Unavailable (Dependency degraded)
When used:
- A critical downstream dependency is degraded (e.g., auth, storage, policy engine, routing metadata) and requests cannot be served reliably.

Primary message (short):
- "Service temporarily unavailable due to a dependency issue. Please retry."

Expanded message (docs/support):
- "A required internal component is currently unavailable. Please retry with exponential backoff. If the issue persists, contact Support with the correlation_id."

Status page wording:
- "We are experiencing elevated errors due to an internal dependency disruption affecting the Hosted API."

D) 400/422 Client validation errors (unchanged; NOT overload)
Messaging should not mention overload protection.

E) 504 Gateway Timeout (we should reduce these)
Target: As overload protection rolls out, we expect fewer timeouts and more explicit 429/503. If customers still see timeouts, Support guidance should say:
- "If you consistently see timeouts, capture correlation IDs and contact Support; this may indicate a regional issue or an upstream networking problem."

Proposed JSON error payload wording (customer-facing)
We will keep payload JSON-compatible and additive.

Example: 503 overload
{
  "error": {
    "type": "overload_error",
    "code": "service_overloaded",
    "message": "Service temporarily overloaded. Please retry after a short delay.",
    "correlation_id": "req_01J...",
    "retry_after_ms": 1200
  }
}
Header: Retry-After: 1

Example: 429 rate limit
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate_limit_error",
    "code": "rate_limit_exceeded",
    "message": "Request rate limit exceeded. Please retry after a short delay.",
    "correlation_id": "req_01J..."
  }
}
Header: Retry-After: 2

Notes / constraints
- Keep “message” stable and not overly specific to internal causes.
- “correlation_id” is required for Support workflows.
- Retry-After MUST be present for overload and rate limiting where we want clients to pause. (See SUP-2860: missing header on some routes.)

Recommended client guidance (copy for docs)
Short version (for quickstarts):
- "On 429/503 responses with a Retry-After header, wait for the indicated delay and retry using exponential backoff with jitter."

Long version (for docs):
- "Implement exponential backoff with jitter for retries (for example: 250ms, 500ms, 1s, 2s… capped), and stop retrying after a fixed time budget. Always honor the Retry-After header when present. Avoid immediate parallel retries, which can amplify congestion."

Idempotency note (copy for docs):
- "If you retry requests that create side effects (e.g., stored outputs or async jobs), use idempotency keys to prevent duplicate work."

Streaming note (copy for docs):
- "For streaming requests, overload errors may occur before the first token is produced. Clients should treat this as a normal retryable failure if accompanied by Retry-After."

Feature reduction / graceful degradation messaging (if/when enabled)
We may temporarily apply protective limits (e.g., lower max_tokens caps, restrict concurrency for streaming, disable selected optional features) under extreme load.
Customer-facing language (docs + status page):
- "To preserve service availability during elevated load, we may temporarily enforce stricter limits on certain request parameters."

Avoid:
- “We disabled tool calling” (too specific). If we must specify, we should gate behind a feature flag and coordinate comms.

Status page templates

Template 1 — Investigating (overload)
Title: "Increased 503 responses (temporary overload)"
Body:
"We are investigating increased error rates for the Redwood Hosted API. Some requests may fail with 503 responses indicating temporary overload. We recommend clients retry with exponential backoff and respect the Retry-After header. Next update in 30 minutes."

Template 2 — Identified (capacity/regional)
Title: "Elevated request rejections in <region>"
Body:
"We identified elevated load impacting a subset of requests in <region>. Our overload protection may reject a portion of traffic to maintain overall reliability and latency. Mitigation is in progress. Clients should retry with backoff and honor Retry-After."

Template 3 — Monitoring (resolved)
Title: "Mitigation applied for elevated overload errors"
Body:
"Mitigation has been applied and we are monitoring recovery. Error rates have returned toward baseline. We will continue to observe and provide a final update after stability is confirmed."

Template 4 — Dependency disruption
Title: "Hosted API disruption due to internal dependency"
Body:
"We are investigating an internal dependency disruption causing elevated errors. Some requests may return 503 responses. Clients can retry with exponential backoff."

Rollout communication plan (draft)

Phase 0 — Internal readiness (before any customer-facing comms)
- Confirm stable error_code + message text across gateway/routes (ENG-4822).
- Support macro draft + escalation checklist (Dev Patel + Owen Phillips).
- Docs page updates ready but not yet published (Elliot + Wei).

Phase 1 — Dark launch / limited canary (no proactive external announcement)
- Canary in one region + subset of tenants.
- Customer-facing behavior change: fewer timeouts, more explicit 429/503 with Retry-After.
- Support readiness: if a customer asks “why did errors change?”, we respond with the short explanation (see Support macro below).

Phase 2 — Publish docs + changelog entry (recommended)
Changelog copy (draft):
- "Improved overload handling for the Hosted API: during elevated load, the API may return explicit retryable 429/503 errors with Retry-After headers instead of timing out. See docs for recommended backoff and retry behavior."

Docs updates:
- Add “Overload errors and retry guidance” section to Hosted API docs.
- Provide code snippets (Python + TypeScript) for backoff/jitter and Retry-After.

Phase 3 — Proactive outreach for enterprise accounts (selective)
- For customers with strict SLOs / high-volume integrations, send a brief note:
  - What’s changing (clearer overload errors)
  - What they should do (respect Retry-After, backoff)
  - How to get help (Support + correlation IDs)

Support macro (draft)
Subject: "About 503 ‘Service temporarily overloaded’ responses"
Body:
"You may see 503 responses with a message indicating temporary overload. This is part of our reliability improvements to protect the Hosted API during traffic spikes. These errors are retryable. Please implement exponential backoff with jitter and honor the Retry-After header when present. If you continue to see elevated errors, share correlation IDs (request IDs) and the approximate timestamps/region/model with us so we can investigate."

Open questions / TODO
- Confirm final external error_code strings with Engineering (ADR-014 alignment). Do we want “service_overloaded” vs “overloaded”? (Prefer explicit + stable.)
- Should we include retry_after_ms in body in addition to Retry-After header? (Engineering leaning yes for SDK ergonomics; ensure header remains source-of-truth.)
- Dedicated tier wording: do we want a separate message that points to “capacity limits configured for your deployment”? (May cause confusion; propose keeping same message but Support playbook differentiates.)
- For fallback routing customers: decide whether to mention fallback occurred (header? response field?) vs silent. For now: silent; document as configuration-level feature.

Notes from recent feedback
- Support: customers strongly prefer actionable retry guidance and correlation IDs over generic 5xx.
- SRE: emphasize that fast rejections are intentional to prevent long tail latency.
- Docs: keep the top-level explanation short; push details into a dedicated page and SDK examples.
